name: Composite
intent: Treat single objects and groups of objects through the same interface, so trees can be handled uniformly.
scenario: A file explorer has files and folders. Folders hold files and other folders. The total size of anything, file or folder, is one call.
problem: Folders contain files and other folders, to any depth. Client code that asks for a total size has to check whether each item is a file or a folder and recurse by hand, everywhere it is needed.
solution: Give files and folders one shared interface with getSize(). A file returns its own size. A folder returns the sum of calling getSize() on its children, which may themselves be folders. The client just calls getSize() on whatever it holds.
pain: Client code checks the type of every item
Recursion over folders is repeated in each feature
Adding a new kind of item means touching every type check
Client must know the tree's structure
benefits: One call, getSize(), works on a file or a whole tree
New item types (shortcut, archive) just implement the interface
Client treats leaves and groups the same
whenToUse: Your data forms a tree: menus, file systems, UI components, org charts
Clients should treat single items and groups uniformly
Operations naturally recurse over the structure
whenNotToUse: The structure is flat: a plain list is enough
Leaves and groups have very different operations, so a shared interface becomes awkward
You need strong type safety on which nodes can have children
pitfalls: Interface bloat: leaves inherit add() and remove() they cannot use
Cycles: a folder containing itself makes getSize() loop forever
Deep trees can overflow the stack on recursion
Hard to restrict what a composite may contain

roles.label: Component
roles.description: Common interface for leaves and composites.

roles.label: Leaf
roles.description: An item with no children that does the real work.

roles.label: Composite
roles.description: Holds children (any Component) and delegates to them.
